name: Global Last Callers
description: Who has called every BBS on the scenewall, and this board's place among them

settings.label: Scenewall server
settings.help: Where the global list comes from. Every AmiExpress board sends its callers to the same place.

settings.label: Seconds to wait
settings.help: Seconds to wait for the server. A caller waits this long at most; the screen is drawn either way.

settings.label: Retries
settings.help: How many times a failed fetch is tried again before the door gives up and draws what it has.

settings.label: Working file
settings.help: Where the 68K viewer spooled the server's answer. Kept so both doors can share one config file.

settings.label: Callers to show
settings.help: AUTO sizes the list to the caller's own screen - their display lines less the eighteen rows of chrome, which is what the original does. A number asks the server for exactly that many.

settings.label: Clear the screen first
settings.help: YES clears the caller's screen before the list. The clear rides on the first logo line, as the original sends it.

settings.label: Style
settings.help: 1 to 4, or a comma-separated list for a random pick each call - the logos below are numbered to match.

settings.label: Centre the name column
settings.help: 1 centres the name column, padding it out to 21 characters a space at a time.

settings.label: Time zone
settings.help: Windows naming, because the scenewall server is what reads it.

settings.label: Scramble the list into place
settings.help: The rows arrive as noise and stop on their real characters while the scenewall is asked. NO draws them once, which is what a very slow line wants.

settings.label: Logo, style 1
settings.help: Five lines of ANSI above the title bar. Draw a 40-column version beside it and a C64 caller reads that instead.

settings.label: Logo, style 2
settings.help: Five lines of ANSI above the title bar. Draw a 40-column version beside it and a C64 caller reads that instead.

settings.help: Five lines of ANSI above the title bar. Draw a 40-column version beside it and a C64 caller reads that instead.
